paragraphs.source_en:
22 Ode to the West Wind
Published as one of the Miscellaneous Poems in 1820. The first three stanzas are drafted
in pencil on ff. 4r rev.–6r rev. of Nbk 12. S. probably made this draft outdoors in the ‘wood
that skirts the Arno’, which he identifies as the place where the ‘poem was conceived and
chiefly written’ in his prose note to the title; that is, in the wooded park of the Cascine
outside the city walls of Florence. He writes to the Gisbornes on 6 November of his liking
for this place where ‘I often walk alone watching the leaves & the rising and falling of the
Arno’ (L ii 150). The first three stanzas he transcribed with slight revisions into Nbk 11
63–5 beneath the date ‘Octr 25’. The greater part of stanza four is drafted on p. 155 of the
same nbk, while all of that stanza and the final five lines of stanza five are found in a mix-
ture of fair copy and draft in Nbk 14 137–8. What appears to be a rejected line is cancelled
